d12.conflict.title: Conflict hunks
d12.conflict.notMerge: Two sides plus the patch preimage — not a merge result. Core computes no merge base and resolves nothing here, so there is no merged text and no resolve action.
d12.conflict.truncated: Over Core's byte bound: at least one file's hunks were dropped.
d12.conflict.omitted: Hunks not shown — this file's lines were over Core's byte bound.
d12.conflict.noHunks: Core listed this file with no hunks.
d12.conflict.noFiles: Core published conflict content naming no file.
d12.conflict.ours: OURS · the Lane's current file, from line {line}
d12.conflict.theirs: THEIRS · the incoming patch, from line {line}
d12.conflict.base: BASE · what the patch expected to find
d12.conflict.base.absent: This hunk carried no preimage at all.
d12.conflict.base.empty: The patch expected an empty region here.
d12.conflict.emptySide: Core read no lines on this side.
d12.conflict.reason.context_mismatch.rem: The preimage was not found in the file. The origin Lane has to re-derive its patch against the current content; nothing can be applied from here.
d12.conflict.reason.already_applied.reme: The file already holds this hunk's new side at that range, so there is nothing left to apply.
d12.conflict.reason.file_missing.remedy: The patch changes a file that is not in the target tree. This is a file-level decision, not a hunk-level one.
d12.conflict.reason.file_deleted.remedy: The deletion's preimage does not account for the whole file, so the file would be left behind. This is a file-level decision.
d12.conflict.reason.binary.remedy: Core reported the content as non-text, so there are no lines to match.
d12.conflict.reason.unnamed.remedy: This build does not name Core's reason, so it is shown exactly as Core published it.
d12.conflict.absent.record: Core published no structured conflict content for this bounce. A bounce an operator raised with a reason has no failed apply behind it and carries none by contract.
d12.conflict.absent.capability: Core publishes no structured conflict content ({capability}), so the conflicting hunk cannot be shown.

d4.step.role.lead: The preset is the role model Core has: coder, reviewer, tester. Branch and worktree are resolved by Core from the reviewed request.

d4.step.skills.lead: Skills and context injection, as the design's third step draws them.
d4.step.gates.lead: Gate policy is code: Core resolves it from the repository and this step is a read-only preview of what it resolved.
d4.seed.note: The task names the Lane and its branch. It travels to Core as the bound Agent's task when an agent is picked on step 2, and as the first message once the Lane is open when none is.

d4.agent.note: Core carries the agent on StarterLaneRequest (runtime.starter_lane_agent): the adapter, and the task from New Lane when there is one. Creation never fails because a session did not start, so step 4 states what became of it.

d15.owner.unnamed: owner Core named no id for
d15.sections.none: The author wrote no sections for this plan.
d15.steps.none: This revision carries no step, so there is nothing to hand off.
d15.record.rule: One open plan per owner; every revision is a durable Core fact.
d15.record.none: Core holds no plan record for this owner.
d15.record.revisionNote: The record carries the latest revision only. Core's durable log keeps every earlier one; this view never reconstructs them.
d15.record.foot: Accepting or rejecting writes an audit row before the decision is announced. Handing off builds one task per step, keeps the dependencies, and runs the DAG Core already owns — the plan never executes itself.
d15.empty.head: No plan proposed
d15.empty.body: Core holds no plan for this owner. Ask in Plan mode and the planner writes one with update_plan; it appears here the moment the first revision is proposed.
d15.empty.planMode: Plan mode blocks file, shell, Git, memory and task mutations.
d15.unavailable.head: Plan documents are unavailable
d15.unavailable.body: Core publishes no {capability}, so this client holds no plan and can send no decision. Nothing was read.
d15.ambiguous.head: More than one open plan
d15.reject.placeholder: Say what has to change before this plan becomes work…
d15.handoff.openUnavailable: No host is bound, so the fleet board cannot be opened from here.
d15.block.planMode: Handing a plan off starts agent work, which Core refuses while plan mode is active. Accept in Plan, switch to Build, then hand it off.
d15.block.noPlan: Core holds no plan for this owner, so there is nothing to decide.
d15.block.decided: Core already recorded a decision on this revision; propose a new revision to replace it.
d15.block.notAccepted: Only an accepted plan can be handed off.
d15.block.handedOff: This plan already became a DAG; Core hands a plan off once.
d15.block.ambiguous: Core published more than one open plan for this owner; this client will not choose one of them.
d15.block.noSteps: This plan has no step, so a handoff would spawn no work.
d15.block.unknown: Core named a block this build cannot name: {code}.

d16.empty.head: No Lane
d16.empty.body: This workspace has no Lane, so there is no agent session to supervise. Create a Lane and its first session appears here — the board never invents one.
d16.empty.rule: Sessions are always shown under the Lane that owns them.
d16.lane.unpublished: Core published no Lane record for this id
d16.lane.noSessions: no session under this Lane yet
d16.block.capability: Core published no {capability}, so this control cannot be sent.
d16.block.completed: it finished; there is nothing to retry
d16.block.noModel: Core published no model for this session
d16.block.noCoreFact: no runtime fact yet — recorded as a contract request
d16.block.status: Core would refuse this: the session is {status}

d16.events.noCapability: Core published no runtime.audit, so no row can be read for this session

d16.events.conversation: Agent conversation, in Core's order — these messages carry no timestamp
d16.detail.noneHint: pick a session under a Lane on the left
d16.detail.noneBody: With no Lane there is nothing to supervise — the detail pane stays empty rather than showing a placeholder agent.
d16.switch.head: Switch model · two steps
d16.switch.stepOne: End this session. Kill has no grace; Stop keeps it. Either way the step is recorded before the session state changes.
d16.switch.stepTwo: Start again on the model below, loading {session} so the new session keeps the transcript.
d16.switch.foot: Viden has no single switch-model command — this is what actually happens.
d16.note: Pause keeps the session alive and holds what you type; it cancels the prompt in flight and denies the approval that prompt was waiting on. Kill ends it with no grace and discards held input. Both are recorded before the session state changes.
d1.permission.revisedFrom: This request revises {request}; Core re-evaluated the narrowed input and still wants a decision.
d1.permission.editHead: Revise the tool input. Core decides the revision afresh through the same gate.
d1.permission.editNote: Every key travels, including the ones you left alone: Core evaluates the whole input, not a patch of it.
d1.permission.editUnavailable: Core marked this request editable and published no tool input for it, so no revision is offered (D1-EDIT-NO-INPUT).
d1.permission.notEditable: Core does not accept a revision for this tool: only flat text inputs are editable, never a patch body.
d1.permission.scopeNotOffered: Core did not offer a standing rule for this request; high-risk requests and plan mode never get one.
settings.standing.detail: Rules an Always decision installed. They hold across sessions and repositories until revoked.
settings.standing.unavailable: Core publishes no {capability}, so no standing rule can be listed or revoked.
